beats.what: Singur got just over 3 TMC of inflow this year, against a record 237 TMC last year. It now holds 3.246 TMC of its 29.91 TMC capacity. Osman Sagar fell from 3.5 to 2.2 TMC.
beats.why: El Niño weakened the monsoon: Telangana's rainfall is 17% below normal and the Manjeera catchment got almost no rain. Karnataka is in drought too, and is still being told to release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu.
beats.care: Western IT corridor (Singur) and Old City (Osman Sagar) are most exposed. Fix leaks now, store water for supply gaps, and watch for your area's schedule from the water board.

cards.body: Officials fear Singur could run dry within 60 days, by mid-December, and say drinking water needs can't be met from December. The water board is drawing up area-wise plans with an alternative source for each locality. A crop holiday has been declared in the Singur ayacut.

cards.title: Which areas are in the red zone?
cards.body: Over-exploited groundwater: Amberpet, Ameerpet, Asifnagar, Charminar, Golconda, Himayatnagar, Khairatabad, Saidabad. Critical: Bahadurpura, Bandlaguda, Maredpally, Musheerabad, Nampally, Secunderabad, Shaikpet. Supply-wise, the western IT corridor (Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur) leans on Singur, and the Old City on Osman Sagar.

Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka (Oct 24): peak power demand is now 20,018 MW (6,648 MW in 2014). Falling reservoirs cut hydropower, which normally gives ~3,500 MW at night peak. A Cabinet sub-committee is handling the crisis. Farmers with low groundwater are asked not to run motors.
HYDRAA found buildings in Borabanda and Navbharat Nagar pumping water straight out of Madhapur's Sunnam Cheruvu through dozens of hidden pipelines, with borewells drilled in bedrooms and kitchens.

cards.title: Hyderabad vs Bengaluru: who's worse off?
cards.body: Both cities are hit by the same weak monsoon. Hyderabad's local sources (Singur, Osman Sagar) are critically low, so the city leans on Krishna and Godavari water. Bengaluru depends on the Cauvery dams (KRS, Kabini, Harangi, Hemavathi): 49 TMC usable on Oct 2, and Karnataka has asked to release less water to Tamil Nadu. We found no current supply cut announced in Bengaluru.

cards.caption: How long Telangana's water crisis may last
cards.body: CM Revanth Reddy said reservoirs hold under 200 TMC and announced a 4-month work scheme after Sankranti.

tldr: Hyderabad needs ~735 MGD but gets ~585 MGD. Singur holds 3.2 of 29.9 TMC, Telangana's big dams 178.6 of 470 TMC, and 15 of 16 Hyderabad district areas over-draw groundwater. Officials warn of a drinking-water squeeze from December, possibly till July.
watch: Water board's area-wise supply plan (expected before December); Singur levels; whether Karnataka's Cauvery release to Tamil Nadu is cut further.
